chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

The one performing i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in whichever of its houses he wishes; it is the same for him whether he prays in the Mosque or in its houses, and this does not contradict the earlier reports which state that i'tikaf is not valid except in the specific places, because what this report entails is the permissibility of prayer in Mecca outside the Mosque, unlike i'tikaf, and this is not prevented, because in case of necessity, if a person leaves the Mosque in Mecca and the time for prayer enters him, it is permissible for him to pray in whichever place he wishes. But the ruling for other mosques is not like this, because it is not permissible for him to pray until he returns to the Mosque in which he performed i'tikaf, and this indicates that.

key_terms.المَسجِدِ: The Mosque (specifically Al-Masjid al-Haram in this context)

ai.seo_question: Can a person performing i'tikaf in Mecca pray in a house outside the Grand Mosque without invalidating their retreat?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Abd Allah ibn Sinan to resolve the apparent contradiction between general i'tikaf rules and the unique status of Mecca. He explains that while prayer location is flexible in Mecca due to necessity, the act of i'tikaf itself remains strictly bound to the designated sanctuary, distinguishing it from other mosques where leaving invalidates the retreat. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that specific local customs or necessities (like Mecca's layout) do not override the fundamental requirement of staying within the consecrated space for i'tikaf.
